finding: The install enables the built-in Local provider but never assigns it to a user group, so the installed model is invisible in the picker and chat answers 403 ACCESS_DENIED — the user must still visit Settings, which INV-2 forbids.
resolution: Verified against get_for_user (INNER JOIN user_group_llm_providers) and user_has_access_to_provider — both required, no admin bypass. ensureLocalProvider now assigns the default/Users group when the provider has no group, leaves an existing arrangement alone, and reports a human-actionable problem when it cannot.

finding: The seeded row ships enabled but the boot health scan probes it (has_credential_for("none") is true, so the unconfigured-row skip does not cover it) and auto-disables it on any transport failure — an offline first boot permanently defeats INV-5.
resolution: Verified in connection_health.rs: the skip is !has_credential(), and Unhealthy calls disable_repository. The boot scan now also skips built-in anonymous rows, with the reasoning in-code. TEST-21 added and verified RED without the fix (it caught it on a NETWORKED box by asserting the row is never PROBED, not merely still enabled).

finding: TEST-1 asserts row.enabled immediately after boot while a fire-and-forget scan can flip that column — it races the mechanism it polices.
resolution: TEST-21 added: waits past the scan and asserts last_health_check_status stays 'untested', which is deterministic regardless of network state.

finding: The loopback git fixture TEST-4/5/7 depend on is unreachable (clone_repository validates PUBLIC_HTTP_OR_HTTPS unconditionally); and its 401-on-Authorization gate is inoperative anyway, since libgit2 supplies credentials only in response to a challenge.
resolution: Independently found and fixed before this audit landed: the fixture was deleted and INV-1 re-proven at the credential decision point. The auditor's second half — that the fixture's gate could not have worked even if reachable — is a stronger argument for the same conclusion and is recorded in DEC-14.

finding: TEST-6 asserts the model row exists and is enabled but never that it is REACHABLE by a user, so it passes unchanged while the group-assignment gap makes the model unusable.
resolution: TEST-6 now asserts the model is visible via GET /api/user-llm-providers for a non-admin member of the default group — the endpoint the model picker actually reads.

finding: The LFS client carries a 30-minute ABSOLUTE request timeout, capping a 5.68 GB blob at a sustained ~3.2 MB/s floor; below that the default install always fails.
resolution: Verified: Client::builder().timeout(60*30) applies to the whole request incl. the body stream. NOT fixed here — raising it weakens a security bound in shared code that closed a Medium finding, and choosing the minimum supported connection speed for a first-run default is a product call, not mine. Recorded as a known limitation in the design doc + DEC-15 and escalated to the owner in HUMAN_FEEDBACK.

finding: deriveViewState checks the terminal download record BEFORE installing/stage, so a retry renders 'failed' with a live button for the whole provider leg, allowing concurrent orchestrations.
resolution: Corroborated by the correctness angle independently. Ordering inverted so a running orchestration outranks any past outcome; a regression test covers both the provider and runtime legs.

finding: isDefaultModelInstalled ignores `enabled` on both provider and model, so a disabled either still renders 'you can start chatting' — contradicting its own doc.
resolution: Both enabled flags now required, with a unit test and a mounted component test for each half.

finding: The design names seven step states as needing GALLERY coverage; the change registers skip:true entries and proves them in a jsdom mount instead, so none is seen by gate:ui's runtime-health / contrast / visual pass.
resolution: Deliberate, recorded as DEC-16. The onboarding module is crawlOnly and its sibling steps map the same way; a bespoke cassette for one step would diverge from every other Onboarding surface. The states ARE proven, by mounting the real component. Flagged to the owner as the one place the shipped approach differs from the design's wording.

finding: A user lacking llm_local_runtime::versions_read is silently blinded — loadVersions early-returns without error so hasInstalledRuntime reports false, then listAvailable 403s; the Install control is gated only on llm_models::create though the flow needs several more permissions.
resolution: The control now gates on the whole set the flow needs (models::create, providers::edit, providers::assign_groups, runtime versions_read/create/update); a user missing any of them gets the informational panel instead of a button that 403s partway through.

finding: TEST-5 wrapped every assertion in `if !raced_to_completion`, so it passed vacuously whenever the cancel lost the race — the comment claimed a skip that did not exist.
resolution: Already gone: TEST-5 was rewritten before this audit landed to drive a real FAILURE (unconditionally reachable) rather than race a cancel. No conditional remains.

finding: The 'cancelled' view state is unreachable from any real store path — the cancel action removes the row and both load paths filter cancelled out — so its explanatory note never renders.
resolution: Verified against cancelLlmModelDownload, subscribeToDownloadProgress and _loadExistingDownloads. The dead state and its note are removed rather than kept as decoration; cancelling restores the offer, and the test now asserts that.

finding: When the snapshot is absent, waitForRuntimeDownload re-lists versions every 500ms for the full 15-minute deadline — ~1800 requests.
resolution: The server-side re-list is now floored at one per 5s while the local poll stays at 500ms.

finding: findInstalledVersionId matches on engine alone and its result is passed to setDefaultVersion, so the step can promote an unrelated llama.cpp version to system default.
resolution: Now matches the full {engine, version, platform, arch, backend} tuple the step actually requested.

finding: install() has no re-entrancy guard, so two overlapping orchestrations can run concurrently; only the weights leg is de-duplicated, and only server-side.
resolution: Corroborated by the conformance angle's same-root finding. install() now early-returns when already installing; the viewState ordering fix removes the window that made it reachable.

finding: The step store is never reset when the wizard is left — unlike its two siblings — so a stale error re-renders the failure alert on a later, unrelated visit.
resolution: A reset action was added and wired at both sites where OnboardingPage already resets the sibling step stores. It clears only this store — the download stores are deliberately untouched so a transfer survives leaving the wizard (INV-6).

finding: TEST-7's doc claims every client handle is dropped, but drop(instance) drops a serde_json::Value; the body was already consumed and each request builds its own client.
resolution: The doc-comment now states what the test actually proves — that the work reaches its own conclusion with no client interaction — rather than overclaiming a dropped connection.

finding: Nothing verifies the upstream repo path/filename the whole feature hinges on actually exists, so a wrong name would ship green and every real install would 404. (Auditor flagged as unconfirmed from its environment.)
resolution: Verified out of band against the real upstream: `git ls-remote https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF` exits 0 with no credential, and the HF model API lists `Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf` among its 28 files. Both values are CORRECT. The coverage gap is real and cannot be closed by a test (the design forbids hitting real HF), so the verification and its date are recorded in the descriptor and DEC-15.

finding: The read deciding whether an access-control write is needed FAILS OPEN: any error from getGroups was swallowed and treated as 'no groups', so a transient 5xx would grant the provider to the default group and silently widen access.
resolution: Now fails CLOSED — an unreadable arrangement is never overwritten; the step reports what to do instead. My own comment claimed to 'leave an operator's existing arrangement exactly as it is', which the catch defeated. Pinned by a test that rejects the read once and asserts no assignment call.

finding: 'Assigned to no group' was treated as 'never configured' and silently repaired, reversing an administrator's deliberate decision to unassign a provider from every group — the supported way to hide it from users while leaving it enabled.
resolution: The step now grants ONLY as part of provisioning it performed itself: if the provider was already enabled, its arrangement is someone else's and is reported, not overridden. A fresh install (provider disabled) still satisfies INV-2, which is the case that matters.

finding: The group-selection fallback ended in active[0] — alphabetically first among the first 100 — so a deployment with no active is_default group, or >100 groups, could have the provider granted to an arbitrary group such as 'Auditors' or 'Contractors', with no confirmation anywhere in the UI.
resolution: The third fallback is deleted. Only the seeded default group or one named Users; otherwise an honest problem message. A test asserts no assignment happens when neither is present.

finding: The allOf gate omitted groups::read and llm_providers::read, which the flow's own calls require and which are NOT wrapped — so it still rendered an enabled button for a user who would 403 after the provider had already been enabled, leaving a half-applied administrative change.
resolution: Corroborated by the tests-quality angle from the other direction (the e2e grant list). Both added, plus user_llm_providers::read for the reachability read. A drop-one loop now mounts the component once per required permission and names the one that was dropped — verified RED by deleting RuntimeVersionUpdate from the gate.

finding: The step enabled whichever local provider sorted first and then shared THAT provider, so an operator's own custom local provider could be turned on and exposed rather than the seeded built-in one.
resolution: Now prefers the built_in local provider explicitly, with a test asserting it is chosen over a custom one that sorts first.

finding: Defence-in-depth note, explicitly NOT a weakness: built_in and auth_type were verified non-attacker-influenced, so no untrusted row reaches the new skip. Residual: any built-in anonymous row now stays 'untested' forever and a future seeded one inherits that silently.
resolution: No behaviour change — the auditor verified the branch is unreachable from any API path and that last_health_check_status gates nothing. The residual it named is now stated in the code comment so the next reader inherits the reasoning rather than rediscovering it.

finding: The e2e permission set documented as 'everything the install flow touches' omitted groups::read, which the group leg needs — a user granted exactly that set would 403 mid-install with every test green; and no test executes ensureGroupAssignment against a real backend.
resolution: groups::read added to both specs (the omission half was already fixed while this angle ran). The 'never executed against a real backend' half stands and is answered at the tier that can: the client leg is covered by ensureLocalProvider.store.test.ts including the refusal cases, and the server requirement by TEST-6, whose reachability assertion was verified RED by removing the assignment.

finding: usePermission was mocked to ignore its argument, so the test claiming to stand for the whole allOf set proved nothing about which permissions the component gates on — dropping any member left every test green.
resolution: The mock now EVALUATES the expression against a held set, and a loop mounts the component once per required permission with that one withheld. Verified RED by deleting RuntimeVersionUpdate from the component — the loop failed naming exactly that permission.

finding: The re-entrancy guard added in round 1 had no test of any kind.
resolution: install.store.test.ts added: leg ordering, the guard, the unavailable-runtime stop, verbatim problem propagation, and that `installing` is always cleared so the guard cannot latch the step shut.

finding: Both behavioural changes to ensureRuntime — full-tuple version matching and the 5s list throttle — were untested; the file had no test at all.
resolution: ensureRuntime.store.test.ts added. The tuple-matching case seeds an unrelated llamacpp build alongside ours and asserts setDefaultVersion gets OURS — verified RED by restoring engine-only matching. Writing it also exposed a defect in my own first draft (seeding the post-download list upfront short-circuited the leg), which the run caught.

finding: The new reset action and its wiring had no test; the component harness mocked reset but never asserted it.
resolution: reset.store.test.ts added, asserting the whole declared initial state is restored rather than a hand-picked subset. The OnboardingPage WIRING remains untested — see FIX_ROUND-2's stated residual.

finding: 'installed means USABLE' checked only the two enabled flags while the step derived from the ADMIN provider list, so an enabled-but-unshared provider still yielded 'already-installed' — the exact invisible-in-the-picker state this feature exists to prevent.
resolution: The step now derives from the USER-FACING list (GET /user-llm-providers), which the server has already filtered to enabled + group-reachable — so 'installed' means 'the user can actually see it'. A mounted test asserts an empty user list is not reported as installed.

finding: TEST-6's reachability assertion cannot regress against the client leg: the test performs the group assignment itself, so it characterises the server rather than policing ensureGroupAssignment.
resolution: Correct as stated. The overclaiming comment ('the assertion that would have caught the gap') is replaced with an explicit SCOPE note: it proves the assignment is REQUIRED (verified RED by deleting it), and points at ensureLocalProvider.store.test.ts for the client leg.

finding: A test named for 'a DISABLED model or provider' only seeded the disabled-model case; the disabled-provider clause was never mounted.
resolution: Split into three mounted cases — disabled model, disabled provider, and an unreachable (empty user list) provider — since one seeded fixture can only exercise one clause.

finding: A test titled 'prefers the DEFAULT group, then one named Users' never exercised the name fallback — every case it seeded had an is_default group, so only the first preference was checked.
resolution: Split: one case for the default-group preference, one with no is_default group at all for the name fallback.

finding: TEST-21's 10s observation window is narrower than the probe's own 10s client timeout, so on a packet-dropping box — the exact scenario the fix is for — the regression could land just after the loop ends.
resolution: Window widened to 30s, which clears the probe's budget with room. The reasoning (why 'generous' had to be measured against the probe timeout rather than guessed) is now in the test.

finding: REGRESSION FROM ROUND 2: the step derives 'installed' from UserLlmProviders, whose loader strips every provider_type === 'local' row, so the already-installed state is unreachable and a user who already has the model is invited to re-download 5.68 GB.
resolution: Corroborated independently by the patterns angle. Verified in _doLoad.ts:15-17 — that store backs the personal-API-key page and excludes local providers by design. Switched to ModelPicker.providers, the picker's own unfiltered list and the one defaultModelId() reasons over. Introduced by MY round-2 fix; caught only because round 3 audited round 2's diff.

finding: Claims the local model 'becomes your default model' while nothing sets a default, and the picker takes the first enabled model of a name-sorted list where cloud providers sort ahead of Local — so a user who added a cloud key would be silently billed to it.
resolution: REJECTED — the reasoning stops one layer short. The server does order `built_in DESC, name ASC`, but the client re-sorts: modelPicker/actions/loadProviders.ts:21 applies sortProviders(), and sortProviders.ts:7-14 places provider_type === 'local' FIRST, then alphabetical. _firstEnabledModelId iterates that sorted list, so the local model is first and the copy is accurate. No change made; recorded so the claim is not re-raised.

finding: A failed cancel is written to `error`, which the running-download view never renders — so Cancel appears to do nothing — and the text later resurfaces under 'The model couldn't be installed' attached to a Retry that restarts the whole transfer.
resolution: Split into its own `cancelError` field with its own alert, rendered while the transfer is still running. Two findings, one root cause.

finding: A failed context load is silent and renders the plain 'not installed' offer, indistinguishable from a genuine one — inviting a 5.68 GB re-download of a model the user may already have.
resolution: Added a `contextUnavailable` state and an alert that says the screen may be out of date.

finding: No state change is announced to assistive technology, and pressing Install drops focus because the control becomes disabled — a screen-reader user gets no signal that anything happened.
resolution: One polite live region for the whole step, announcing each state as a sentence read out of context. Covers the completion case too, which was likewise silent.

finding: The low-memory advisory renders BELOW the install control, so at ~390px the warning meant to inform the decision arrives after it.
resolution: Moved above the card, with a mounted test asserting document order rather than trusting the source layout.

finding: Users without install permissions are always told an administrator has yet to install the model, even on a deployment where it is installed and waiting in their picker.
resolution: Context is now loaded for every user (its read self-gates on a permission they hold) and the unpermitted branch distinguishes 'installed and ready for you' from 'your administrator installs it'.

finding: A bare 'Cancel' label inside wizard chrome that has its own navigation is ambiguous to a screen-reader user, and a multi-GB transfer is discarded by one unconfirmed click.
resolution: Relabelled 'Cancel download' with an explicit aria-label. The confirmation-dialog half is NOT done — see FIX_ROUND-3's deferred list; it is a product choice about friction, not a defect.

finding: The offer stresses 'runs offline' and 'nothing sent to a provider' without saying the install itself downloads 5.68 GB from Hugging Face.
resolution: The offer copy now states the download source and that it needs an internet connection once — a fair point for a privacy- or bandwidth-conscious reader.

finding: The failure alert prints the raw server/transport error verbatim to a first-run user.
resolution: DEFERRED, not dismissed. Translating git/HTTP failures into user-facing guidance needs a mapping the rest of the app does not have either (the sibling download surfaces show raw reasons too), so inventing one here would diverge from every other download surface. The reason IS shown alongside actionable next steps ('You can retry, or continue'). Recorded for the owner in HUMAN_FEEDBACK.

finding: 'Preparing…' shows no progress and no way out, and can persist up to 15 minutes before failing.
resolution: DEFERRED. The state is announced (live region) and Next is never blocked, so it is not a dead end; adding progress to it needs per-leg reporting the provider/runtime-discovery calls do not expose. Recorded for the owner.

finding: Nothing checks or mentions free DISK space before committing to a 5.68 GB file — only RAM is advised on.
resolution: DEFERRED — genuinely worth having, but there is no disk-space figure on the hardware surface today (it reports memory + GPU), so this needs a backend addition. Recorded for the owner as a follow-up.

finding: hasCompletedDefaultModelDownload and the already-installed branch it feeds are unreachable — a completed DownloadInstance is filtered out by BOTH writers of the downloads array — and this repeats the exact mistake the same file documents avoiding for the `cancelled` state.
resolution: Verified in subscribeToDownloadProgress.ts:95-97 and _loadExistingDownloads.ts. Dead code removed rather than tested. It was also unnecessary: create_model_with_files (the shared helper both the upload and download paths use) publishes SyncEntity::UserLlmProvider on model creation, and the ModelPicker store reloads on sync:user_llm_provider — so the success transition was already wired. That is now stated where the branch used to be.

finding: The allOf gate omits llm_models::read, which loadLlmProviders requires and silently early-returns without — the same silent-early-return class the comment two lines above cites as the reason RuntimeVersionRead is listed.
resolution: Added. Without it the user got an enabled button whose install ended in 'No local provider exists to install into', which is not even the true reason. The drop-one loop now covers it.

finding: UserGroup.list and assignGroupToProvider are unwrapped while the sibling read 16 lines above was just wrapped to fail closed — so a failure escapes as a raw transport string after the provider has already been enabled.
resolution: Both wrapped, each returning the leg's own actionable words and naming the group it tried to use. Consistency on every exit path, as the guidelines require.

finding: A new branch and exported predicate were added to the pure viewState module with no case added to its dedicated unit-test file.
resolution: Moot — the branch and the predicate are gone (see the dead-code finding above). Removing unreachable code is the better answer than testing it.

finding: The call-site permission guard duplicates a gate the callee already performs, so the permission is maintained in two places.
resolution: Guard removed; loadProviders self-gates, which is the repo's convention for shell-eager loads (the gate lives in the action, not the call site).
